relevance_note: Case report of a family with GFAP p.R416W: "She and her daughter’s glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) gene analysis revealed the same heterozygous missense mutation, c.1246C > T, p.R416W"; plus a literature table (Table 2) of asymptomatic GFAP carriers.
method_note: Read the paper by hand; a Python script in scratch only assembled the JSON and transcribed Table 2 rows, checked against the table, and every span was checked verbatim. Labels: the propositus and her daughter use the pedigree labels from the Fig. 1 legend ('Patient III-3', 'patient IV-4'); the mother and maternal aunt have no pedigree label in the text, so rule 2 was used. II-1 ('the family member (II-1) had similar psychological manifestations') gets its own row, but the paper does not say whether II-1 is the mother or the maternal aunt (both generation II); possible duplicate. Mother and aunt were not tested for GFAP (only III-3 and IV-4 'performed the molecular diagnosis'), so no variant rows for them; inheritance for III-3 is not reported. Table 2 (literature asymptomatic carriers): label from the 'Patient Reference' column, whole cell copied into source_reference_in_review; Patients 6 and 10 appear on two rows each (merged cells repeated), treated as one person with two variants each. The 'Age (years)' column is not defined (the footnote says no age at onset is reported for Patients 4 and 10, so it may be onset or examination age), so ages were left not reported for Table 2 patients. Gene symbol for Table 2 variants is not printed in the table; GFAP taken from the surrounding text and Fig. 1 legend. Patient 10 [20] is printed as c.1260C > T p.R416W, whereas the text gives p.R416W as c.1246C > T; recorded as printed. 'Asymptomatic' (Table 2 title, and 'didn’t present with any neurological symptoms' for IV-4) was recorded as 'symptoms' / 'neurological symptoms' excluded but not used to exclude specific checklist symptoms. Thyagarajan [31] woman and son were included (sex and variant given); their variant is 'the above mutation', taken from the preceding sentence naming c.1246C > T, p.R416W; zygosity left not reported because the 'heterozygous' wording is about the variant in other reports. Whole-investigation normals (general medical examination unremarkable, serum laboratory panel unremarkable, MRA normal) were not turned into specific excluded features. Autonomic testing was normal 2 years after onset, but bowel and bladder urgency began at age 31 and the authors state autonomic dysfunction 'was found in our patient'; both recorded, checklist autonomic dysfunction observed (different time points, not treated as a contradiction). Normal mental status was not used to exclude 'cognitive decline'. Palatal myoclonus 'not seen in our patient' used to exclude 'palatal tremor'. No stacked cells in this paper.
